title: Standing on the Rock
summary: Christian reasonableness isn't the agreeableness of someone with no convictions. It is the joy of someone standing firm on the rock of Christ.
exhortation: When I think about this rejoicing and reasonableness, what popped into my head was the California surfer attitude. That kind of reasonableness says, "I agree with you about everything, because I don't really have any convictions. Everything's awesome, bro." That is not what Paul means here. That kind of agreeableness makes my stomach queasy because it's unmoored, like someone on a wildly swaying ship with no center. It isn't based on anything.

Christian reasonableness and rejoicing are totally different. They come from a deeply felt, firm conviction, and the result is almost awe-inspiring. Instead of a ship being tossed around, picture a Christian standing on the rock with waves breaking and roaring all around, smiling.

The difference is where it starts: "Rejoice in the Lord." The Christian whose heart rejoices in the Lord is already happy, not in an uncaring way, but because he has tasted and seen what is most worthy of his whole life's devotion. He isn't chasing anything or running around trying to figure out his purpose. He is solid and firm. Rejoicing always in the Lord is the outward expression of an inward reality: you are standing on the rock of Christ.

That person doesn't get sucked into pointless arguments. He can sniff out a pointless debate a mile away. He is anxious for nothing, fixed and firm, and the peace of God spills out of him into his family, his church and his friends, and draws them into that stability. So this morning, let's ponder what is beautiful. Let our thoughts be filled with the wonders of Jesus, God the Son, who set his affection on you from eternity past and decided to love you. That's worth rejoicing about.
prayer: Lord, show your mighty power in our lives, so that we stand on the rock as Christians: not defeated, not giving in to this world's relativism where nothing matters and nothing is worth caring about. You haven't called us to apathy. You've called us to stand firm on the rock with a smile, trusting you, knowing you advocate for us, you are with us and you are for us, and your mighty arm is not too short to reach us in any circumstance.

Pour out your grace and mercy on us, so that we are fully satisfied and happy in you, and let it overflow into the lives of our families, children, friends, spouses and neighbors, so that the love of Christ overflows from us into the world, just as you intended. Thank you, Jesus. Amen.
